subject: Game Theory
title: The Seller's Advantage
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Seller's Advantage.

hook.text: Auctions benefit sellers by creating urgency. Bidders compete in real time, pushing prices up.

buildup.text: Fixed-price sales leave money on the table. If the buyer would pay more, the seller never knows.

discovery.text: Auctions capture 'consumer surplus'—the gap between what buyers would pay and what they actually pay.

twist.text: But too few bidders kill the advantage. With just one buyer, there's no competition to drive the price.

climax.text: The seller's real power lies in attracting enough bidders to create genuine competitive tension.

quiz.question: What kills the seller's auction advantage?
